messages:
incident-bot: Paging eng-oncall — p99 latency spike detected for customer Ekko (us-west-2). SLOs degraded. Streaming stalls observed, tail latency increase.

incident-bot: Summary metrics: p95 320ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.6s -> 8.3s, active streams from Ekko +380% vs baseline. Alerts: #production-slos, routing-errors. Runbook: /runbooks/streaming-tail

Anya (oncall): ACK. jumping in. seeing a steady rise in concurrent active sessions from ekko-prod key. their session count went from ~120 -> ~580 in last 3m.

Marta: Ekko is on shared hosted pool but pinned to model small-gpt-qa-v2-16k (quantized). They have a high-prefix chat pattern (long system prompt + many short user turns).

Leo: do we have KV cache hit stats? high prefix churn could thrash KV cache and spike tail.

Samir: pulling metrics — kv_cache_hit_rate for pool g-pool-12: 87% -> 41% during spike. cache evictions spiked.

Anya (oncall): yep that explains stalls. streaming actors spending time rebuilding KV. looks like many sessions with different prefixes.

Marta: Any recent deploys in us-west-2?

Infra-Bot: deploy-bot: No production rollouts in us-west-2 in the last 30m.

Leo: immediate mitigation options: 1) route Ekko to a dedicated pool (if capacity) 2) enable aggressive prefix dedupe / prefix cache TTL 3) fallback to shorter-context model variant 4) throttle concurrency per-api-key.

Anya (oncall): checking capacity. we have 2 warm dedicated pools with spare slots but require approval to attach.

Ellis-CS: adding context — Ekko started a marketing campaign this morning, they warned of traffic spike but estimated web traffic not this high. They are open to minor degradations for 10-15m if it buys time.

Samir: I can flip a routing rule to direct Ekko -> dedicated pool ekko-pool-1. will need a temp policy update. anyone object?

Marta: do it. we need fast relief. also drop max_tokens for streaming to 256 for Ekko requests while we stabilize.

Anya (oncall): doing both. patching route now.

Anya (oncall): PATCH /routing/policies/ekko -> {"target_pool":"ekko-pool-1","max_tokens":256,"burst_limit":500} applied.

Anya (oncall): also enabling prefix_dedupe = true for ekko-pool-1 to reduce KV churn.

Infra-Bot: routing change deployed to control plane in 21s.

Samir: starting a rolling drain of 2 nodes in g-pool-12 to reduce pressure but not full restart. command:```bash
kubectl cordon node/g-pool-12-node-07 && kubectl drain node/g-pool-12-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=5m
```

Leo: good. avoid full restarts unless necessary. restarting inference processes might evict warmed kernels.

Anya (oncall): monitoring p95/p99 now. initial numbers: p95 -> 410ms (was 1.2s), p99 -> 760ms (was 8.3s). better but still above SLO.

Marta: confirm streaming stall reduction — any more 400ms+ streaming stalls?

Samir: streaming stall events (per-minute) dropped from 48 -> 6 after route change. KV hit rate on ekko-pool-1 is 92%.

Ellis-CS: Ekko engineering says they can throttle client-side reconnections for 5m. planning to push a small client-side backoff.

Anya (oncall): next steps: keep ekko on dedicated pool, watch for chattiness causing cache thrash, schedule post-incident tuning for prefix dedupe heuristics.

Leo: reminder: we should add an autoscale policy for ekko-pool-1 to allow quick capacity growth next time (temporary burst capacity).

Samir: noted — filing infra task: "enable burst capacity for ekko-pool-1" and linking to runbook.

Anya (oncall): handing this to Samir for the next 45m while I go to another page. Samir, ping me if you see p99 > 1.5s.

Samir: taking it. I'll keep the thread updated. current live snapshot: p95 340ms, p99 630ms, active streams 210 -> stabilizing.

Marta: quick log snippet showing previous stalls:```
[2026-03-15T15:12:23Z] INF stream_conn id=ekko-ck-145 processing latency=8200ms reason=kv_rebuild
[2026-03-15T15:12:24Z] INF stream_chunk id=ekko-ck-145 stall detected at token 14
```

Samir: Applying additional guard: per-key concurrency cap = 20 for Ekko API key. will reduce thundering.

Anya (oncall): good call. keep the client informed (Ellis-CS).

Ellis-CS: told Ekko to enable client backoff + accept temporary per-key cap. They are good with it. :+1:

Samir: per-key cap applied. observing further p99 improvements — down to ~480ms.

Infra-Bot: note: drained node g-pool-12-node-07 rejoined after reprovisioning. no crash loops.

Anya (oncall): Samir — if things stay stable for 30m we'll start epic-level follow-up (tuning runbook, add test for prefix churn). Please escalate if new regression.

Samir: will do. handing back to Anya in 40m. logging incident for postmortem: INC-2026-3798765432.

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated. Please file a P0 or P1 postmortem if root cause unknown.

Anya (oncall): thanks all. final note: root cause likely a sudden customer-driven prefix variety + insufficient prefetched KV capacity combined with no burst pool. action items: add per-customer burst capacity, improve prefix dedupe heuristics, add automated per-key concurrency cap for high-churn customers.

Samir: copying action items to infra board. closing handoff.

Ellis-CS: will follow up with Ekko CS notes and customer impact summary (they saw ~8min degraded UX).

Anya (oncall): closing thread — if anyone needs logs or raw metrics I'll upload to the incident folder. :white_check_mark:
